title: 14-day activation cheatsheet - Hubster integration
body:
Purpose
----
Quick operational guide for the Hubster POC (14-day activation window). This is a working doc intended for the SE + Hubster technical leads. Objective: get a minimal, customer-facing integration live and validated in two weeks so CS can start pilot usage and collect qualitative feedback.

High-level goals (what "success" looks like at day 14)
- Functional: Hubster app can call Redwood inference endpoint for customer-facing summarization workflow (end-to-end test from Hubster UI to inference result).
- Perf: P50 latency <= 350ms for typical user prompt (<= 512 token context), P95 <= 800ms in steady load.
- Throughput: sustain 30 qps in a single Dedicated instance config or via hosted fallback with <5% error rate.
- Cost target: average inference cost per session falls below $0.025/session (measured on tokens + compute estimate).
- Security & compliance: TLS mutual auth on private deployment or verified insecure data handling acceptance if using hosted with CIS controls.
- Qualitative: internal product manager signs off on usability of responses in 3 sample user flows.

Scope (explicitly in scope)
- Onboarding: auth config, routing rules, model pinning for the POC model, minimal prompt templates.
- Observability: basic dashboard (latency, errors, token usage) and trace link from Hubster request -> Redwood request id.
- Rollout policy: canary 10% then 100% (manual) for Hubster dev org.
- Evals: 50 prompt set to measure first-pass quality and regression compared to baseline.

Out of scope for 14 days
- Full production SSO integration (defer to dedicated engagement), advanced cost-optimization (quantization experimentation), long-term data retention policies.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90m)
- 00:00 - 00:10 Introductions & success alignment (Maya)
- 00:10 - 00:25 Architecture walkthrough (Hubster infra lead)
- 00:25 - 00:45 Redwood runtime + routing overview + recommended model (Diego)
- 00:45 - 01:00 Integration patterns (webhook vs proxy) + auth options (Priya)
- 01:00 - 01:15 Success metrics, monitoring plan, and acceptance tests (Omar)
- 01:15 - 01:30 Next steps, owners, and immediate blockers

Deployment assumptions
- Hubster will provide a staging API key and a small staging dataset (10k tokens) for eval runs by day 3.
- Network: Hubster dev environment reachable from Redwood staging IPs; if not, we'll use an SSH tunnel for initial tests.
- Model: use rwd-7B-instruct (non-quantized) for initial quality baseline. If latency or cost is an issue, fallback to rwd-7B-8bit quantized variant.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
1) Functional acceptance (owner: Hubster PM)
   - 10 sample end-to-end flows produce acceptable outputs (score >= 3/5 by PM rubric)
   - Error rate < 2% on a 500 request smoke test
2) Performance acceptance (owner: SE lead)
   - P50 <= 350ms and P95 <= 800ms measured during a 10-minute steady-state load (30 qps)
   - No memory leaks or server-side errors >0.5% of requests
3) Observability acceptance (owner: Observability engineer)
   - Request-level tracing enabled; dashboards show token counts, latency histograms, and per-route error rates
4) Security acceptance (owner: security reviewer)
   - TLS + auth validation completed; any data-handling exceptions documented and accepted by Hubster legal

Runbook & rollback criteria
- If error rate exceeds 5% for 5 consecutive minutes during test, automatically revert routing to hosted fallback model.
- If P95 > 1.2s for longer than 10 minutes, pause canary and notify oncall SRE (Leah Park).
- Escalation path: SE -> SRE -> Platform eng -> CS director (see contact list below).

Open questions (to resolve by day 2)
- Hubster: which environments need sampling logs exported (dev only or prod-equivalent staging)?
- Data residency: is any prompt/response PII-sensitive that needs special handling? (Hubster legal)
- Authentication: prefer signed JWT or mutual TLS for POC? If JWT, who issues tokens?
- Load profile: are user flows bursty (short spikes) or steady streams? Need sample traffic trace.

Immediate action items (owner - ETA)
- Hubster: provide staging API key and small sample dataset (Hubster dev lead - Day 1)
- SE: create test harness and run 500-request smoke test (Diego - Day 2)
- Infra: open temporary ingress rule from Hubster IPs to Redwood staging (Priya - Day 1)
- Observability: deploy minimal dashboard + trace link (Omar - Day 3)
- Legal/Security: sign POC data handling note (Maya + Hubster legal - Day 5)

Measurement table (track each day)
- Day | Total requests | Avg tokens/request | P50 ms | P95 ms | Error % | Cost estimate
- Day 1 | 0 | - | - | - | - | -
- Day 3 | 500 | 120 | 310 | 720 | 1.2% | $12
- Day 7 | 3,500 | 115 | 290 | 650 | 0.9% | $65
- Day 14 | 15,000 | 110 | 320 | 700 | 0.7% | $270

Notes to self / workshop sidebars
- Try the proxy pattern first (smaller change for Hubster engineers) then move to direct SDK integration once auth is stable.
- Keep the prompt templates in a single repo under github.com/hubster/poc-prompts for easy iteration and evals.
- Schedule a 15m daily stand during first 5 days to accelerate unblockings.

Appendix: contacts

End of doc
